scenario.prompt_to_agent:
router11 (one of the OSPF spokes) shows no routing path to
external networks. Operators report router11 has OSPF Full
adjacencies but cannot ping the Campus 2 server-side SVI
(10.5.0.254). Other spokes (router10, router8) reach it fine.
Find the difference on router11.

injection.command: ip route del default 2>/dev/null; vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "no default-information originate" -c "exit" -c "exit" 2>/dev/null

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router11 default route
Mechanism: router11 originally had a default route (either
  static or learned via OSPF default-information). When
  removed, any destination not explicitly in router11's RIB
  has no next hop. OSPF adjacencies stay up because they
  use directly-connected links, but transit to 10.5.0.254
  (which is reachable only via the default + intermediate
  hops) fails.
Localization: router11
Root cause: default route removed on router11
Fix: `ip route add default via <next-hop>` or re-enable
  default-information learning
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip route add default via <next-hop>` or re-enable
  default-information learning

agent.diagnosis_text:
No fault is present in the network. The reported symptom — that router11 cannot
ping the Campus 2 SVI at 10.5.0.254 while other spokes can — does not match the
observed state of the network.

All diagnostic evidence confirms router11 is healthy:
(1) OSPF adjacencies: router11 holds two Full adjacencies — one to router17
(ID 192.168.144.2 via 10.1.0.2) and one to router1 (ID 192.168.10.2 via
10.1.1.1) — consistent with the other spokes.
(2) Routing table: 10.5.0.0/24 is correctly installed as an OSPF route
([110/20] via 10.1.0.2 eth0), with the cost matching the expected two-hop
path through router17.
(3) OSPF LSDB: the router-LSA and network-LSA checksum totals on router11
(0x0004f9b1 / 0x0005008b) are identical to those on router10, confirming no
missing or stale LSA.
(4) Data-plane: a live ping from router11 to 10.5.0.254 delivered 4/4 packets
with zero loss; traceroute confirms the two-hop path (router17 → sshswitch br_v5).
(5) No access-lists, iptables rules, policy-routing rules, or OSPF distribute-lists
exist on router11.

The ticket describes a false premise: the condition the operator observed either
resolved on its own before investigation began (e.g., transient OSPF convergence
during lab startup) or was never accurate. The corrective action is to close the
incident — no configuration change is required.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names and discusses router11 as the device under investigation throughout the diagnosis.
The agent's writeup does not mention or identify the default route on router11 (the required affected component), instead asserting no fault.

The agent explicitly rules out an OSPF neighbor failure by citing Full adjacencies, matching LSDB checksums, and correct OSPF-learned routes, thereby distinguishing the fault from an OSPF neighbor issue.
The agent recommends no configuration change (close the incident), which does not address the expected fix of adding a default route or re-enabling default-information learning.

The agent's investigation produced concrete observations (OSPF neighbors, route presence, successful ping/traceroute, ip_forward and no ACLs) that directly support its conclusion; its inferences follow logically and the checks cover plausible alternative causes.
